sentences.text: The genus Azhdarcho was established by Lev A. Nesov in 1984, with the type species designated as Azhdarcho lancicollis.
Most individuals possessed a wingspan ranging from 3 to 4 meters, although some fossil remains indicate spans reaching 5 to 6 meters.
Nesov described the neck vertebrae of this species as extremely elongated and round in cross-section at their mid-length.
Lev A. Nesov discovered Azhdarcho fossils in the Kyzyl Kum desert between 1974 and 1981.

The type specimen, catalog number TsNIGRmuzey 1/11915, consists of a single anterior neck vertebra, while twelve paratypes include additional neck vertebrae, wing and leg elements, and jaw pieces deposited at the F.N. Chernyshev Central Geologic Exploration Museum in St. Petersburg.
Nesov noted that the articulation of Azhdarcho's vertebrae resulted in very limited neck flexibility, meaning the animal could not rotate its neck but could only flex it vertically to some degree.
Nesov suggested Azhdarcho may have fed like a modern skimmer, scooping prey from the water surface with its long neck.
However, studies by Mark Witton suggest that azhdarchids like Azhdarcho were likely terrestrial stalkers similar to storks or ground hornbills.

Nesov erected the subfamily Azhdarchinae within the family Pteranodontidae based on shared characteristics with Azhdarcho, initially placing Quetzalcoatlus and Arambourgiania in this group before it was later reclassified as the family Azhdarchidae.
Azhdarcho is the type genus of the family Azhdarchidae and is placed within the clade Neoazhdarchia.
Azhdarcho lived about 92 million years ago in Uzbekistan during the middle Turonian stage of the late Cretaceous.
The genus lived from the Turonian to the Campanian stages, spanning between 93.9 and 72.2 million years ago.
Recent research suggests that large pterosaurs like Azhdarcho were probably not capable of skimming due to high energy and anatomical requirements.
